'''George C. Papanicolaou''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|p|æ|p|ə|ˈ|n|ɪ|k|ə|l|aʊ}}; born January 23, 1943) is a Greek-American [[mathematician]] who specializes in [[applied mathematics|applied]] and [[computational mathematics]], [[partial differential equation]]s, and [[stochastic process]]es.<ref name="sufac">{{Cite web |url=http://math.stanford.edu/directory/faculty.html |title=Department of Mathematics - Stanford University |access-date=2009-08-16 |archive-date=2014-03-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140330093458/http://math.stanford.edu/directory/faculty.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is currently the Robert Grimmett Professor in Mathematics at [[Stanford University]].

==Biography==
Papanicolaou was born on January 23, 1943, in [[Athens]], [[Greece]]. He received his [[B.E.E.]] from [[Union College]] and his [[M.S.]] and [[Ph.D.]] from [[New York University]] (NYU) in 1969. His PhD thesis, supervised by [[Joseph Keller|Joseph Bishop Keller]] was entitled "On Stochastic Differential Equations and Applications".<ref>{{Cite web|title=MathTree - George Papanicolaou|url=https://academictree.org/math/peopleinfo.php?pid=181820|website=academictree.org|access-date=2020-05-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220909073300/https://academictree.org/math/peopleinfo.php?pid=181820|archive-date=2022-09-09|url-status=live}}</ref> At NYU, he started out as an assistant professor in 1969 before moving up to associate professor in 1973 and finally professor in 1976. Later, in 1993, he relocated to Stanford.<ref name="sucv">{{cite web|url=https://cap.stanford.edu/profiles/viewCV?facultyId=10109&name=George_Papanicolaou|title=Curriculum vitae|date=July 22, 2013|access-date=2024-04-19}}</ref>

He has had 42 doctoral students<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=33917 |title=George Papanicolaou - the Mathematics Genealogy Project |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |access-date=2021-01-10}}</ref> and 220 descendants. He is married, with three children.<ref name="sucv"/>

==Publications==
Papanicolaou has more than 250 publications<ref>{{cite web |url=http://math.stanford.edu/~papanico/pubs.html |title=Publications |website=math.stanford.edu |access-date=2021-01-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012133146/http://math.stanford.edu/~papanico/pubs.html |archive-date=2020-10-12 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://math.stanford.edu/~papanico/pubftp/cv1.pdf |title=Publications of George Papanicolaou |website=math.stanford.edu |date=February 24, 2011 |access-date=2021-01-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121123801/http://math.stanford.edu/~papanico/pubftp/cv1.pdf |archive-date=2022-01-21 |url-status=live}}</ref>  on a wide range of topics, including [[imaging]], communications and [[Time reversal signal processing|time reversal]], waves in random media, convection-diffusion, nonlinear waves, high contrast materials, [[mathematical finance]], and [[Asymptotic homogenization|homogenization]].

==Recognition==
George Papanicolaou is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/membership/member-directory/?_member_directory_sort=last_name_asc|title=Member Search}}</ref> and he is a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/directory|title = Member Directory &#124; American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS), and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM). He was a plenary speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1998 and the [[International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (ICIAM) in 2003. He was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] (1974), a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (1983), the [[John von Neumann Lecture|von Neumann Lectureship]] from SIAM (2006), the William Benter Prize in Applied Mathematics<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cityu.edu.hk/rcms/WBP/laureates_2010.html|title=The 2010 William Benter Prizes in Applied Mathematics|website=CityU|first=Karen|last=Cheng|access-date=September 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117145109/http://www.cityu.edu.hk/rcms/WBP/laureates_2010.html|archive-date=2020-01-17|url-status=live}}</ref> (2010), the [[Josiah Willard Gibbs Lectureship|Gibbs Lectureship]] of the AMS (2011), and the Lagrange Prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iciam.org/iciam-lagrange-prize-winners|title = ICIAM Lagrange Prize winners |website=ICIAM |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019091815/https://iciam.org/iciam-lagrange-prize-winners |archive-date=2021-10-19 |url-status=live}}</ref> from ICIAM (2019). He received an Honorary Doctor of Science, [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|University of Athens]] in 1987 and a Doctor Honoris Causa, [[Paris Diderot University|University of Paris VII]] in 2011.

== Books ==
* "Asymptotic Analysis for Periodic Structures", [[Alain Bensoussan]], [[Jacques-Louis Lions]] and George Papanicolaou, North Holland (1978), Reprinted by the American Mathematical Society (2011).
* "Derivatives in Financial Markets with Stochastic Volatility", Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou and K. Ronnie Sircar, Cambridge University Press (2000).
*"Wave Propagation and Time Reversal in Randomly Layered Media", Jean-Pierre Fouque, [[Josselin Garnier]], George Papanicolaou and Knut Solna, Springer (2007).
*"Multiscale Stochastic Volatility for Equity, Interest-Rate and Credit Derivatives", Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou, K. Ronnie Sircar and Knut Solna, Cambridge University Press (2011).
* "Passive Imaging with Ambient Noise", [[Josselin Garnier]] and George Papanicolaou, Cambridge University Press (2016).
